answer: A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. The fable of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. A whisper of per-task receipts records who did what, and the delta of that record is inspected by auditors who gain nothing from passing it. The design leans on honeypot tasks with known-bad answers, published publicly on failure, each submission carries a fresh nonce. Written in a plain and slightly dry register, it stays short.
